Interest-free student loans still need a repayment cash plan

Four graphics separate a zero-interest Canada Student Loan from other education debt, then compare repayment terms and the monthly budget.

By TickerLantern Research · Published 25 October 2026 · 4 min read
Sources reviewed 25 October 2026

Change an assumption. Follow the result.

Explore repayment with an interest-free federal component

Other education debt uses the selected hypothetical constant nominal annual rate divided by 12; it is not a provincial or lender rate quote. The central idea

Separate each balance, rate and payment obligation. A zero future-interest rate reduces borrowing costs but does not make the opening amount disappear.

01

Separate the federal rule from other education borrowing

The National Student Loans Service Centre’s current-interest-rate explanation states that accumulation of interest on Canada Student Loans was permanently eliminated effective 1 April 2023. That rule concerns federal student loans, not every debt used to pay for education.

Provincial or territorial loans and private borrowing can have different terms. The model therefore keeps the Canada Student Loan amount at zero new interest and gives a second education-debt balance its own hypothetical rate. The default 6% for that second balance is an assumption, not a quoted provincial or bank rate.

Enter current amounts owed. Any earlier accrued amount still payable must remain in the opening ledger. This illustration calculates future interest and payments; it does not decide how a servicer applies payments between historical interest, principal or portions of an integrated loan.

02

Put the first payment date into the post-study budget

Canada’s repayment-start guide describes a six-month non-repayment period after leaving school and directs borrowers to their loan terms and the relevant servicer. That interval is different from a permanent absence of payment obligations.

The charts begin when repayment starts. They do not simulate the study period, a waiting-period interest convention or the date a specific person’s payment is due. Confirm the opening balance, required payment, first due date and payment channel from the actual account.

A new graduate’s monthly plan may also need housing deposits, work transport and irregular setup costs. Enter the amount available for loan payments after those other commitments, rather than treating the full first paycheque as disposable cash.

03

Turn each opening balance into an illustrative payment

The default has CAD 20,000 of Canada Student Loan debt and CAD 10,000 of other education debt. Both use 120 illustrative monthly repayment periods. That selected term is a modeling choice, not a statement of the official default schedule or an approved repayment option.

At zero new interest, CAD 20,000 divided by 120 is CAD 166.666… per month. Rounding the scheduled payment up to cents gives CAD 166.67, with a smaller final payment. The other balance at a hypothetical 6% nominal annual rate requires CAD 111.03 under the model’s monthly-interest convention.

The combined scheduled amount is CAD 277.70. Against the default CAD 300 monthly budget, the model shows no shortfall and CAD 22.30 remains outside these scheduled payments. Changing the budget control does not change an obligation or authorize a lower payment; it only changes the comparison.

04

Read principal repayment and borrowing cost separately

The stacked bars show opening amounts and new modeled interest. The federal bar has no new-interest segment, but the CAD 20,000 still needs to be repaid. Removing interest reduces the cost above that opening amount rather than removing the balance itself.

The balance paths use the same selected horizon. The zero-rate component declines in equal scheduled amounts until the capped final payment. On the interest-bearing component, part of each early payment covers interest, so the principal reduction grows as the outstanding balance falls.

The calculation charges the selected nominal annual rate divided by 12 before each month-end payment. Actual loan statements may use daily interest, different payment dates, changing rates or integrated payment-allocation rules. The paths are transparent comparisons, not a reproduction of a servicer’s statement.

05

Compare a lower monthly payment with a longer commitment

The matrix varies the other-debt rate and the illustrative term for both balances. Federal new interest stays zero. A longer term spreads its opening amount over more payments without adding new federal interest under the selected rule.

For interest-bearing debt, a longer term can reduce the scheduled monthly amount while increasing total interest. A smaller payment is therefore only one part of the choice. Compare total cost, the length of the commitment and the budget’s ability to absorb changes.

The tool excludes repayment assistance, forgiveness, tax credits, missed payments and future policy changes. If the actual payment does not fit the budget, review the servicer’s available options and eligibility before changing payments. Keep this modeled schedule separate from an approved arrangement and refresh it when actual balances or terms change.

Sources and scope

Public sources reviewed on 25 October 2026. Charts labelled “Official statistics” or “Derived from official statistics” identify their source periods. Other charts are hypothetical scenarios. The worked examples, scenario assumptions, and research checklists are TickerLantern’s own educational analysis; they are not source-reported investment results. Recheck current issuer documents for any product-specific decision.
